# Multi-scale and Mip-aware Representations

Also called: Mip-aware Training Configurations

## Overview
This family encompasses training configurations for neural radiance fields that explicitly address aliasing and multi-scale reconstruction artifacts through specialized input encodings, activation functions, or supersampling strategies. It distinguishes itself from standard NeRF configurations by modifying the optimization loop to handle frequency content and resolution mismatches, rather than relying solely on geometric primitives. It builds on [Method-Specific Training Configurations](6267-method-specific-training-configurations.md).

## Shared principles
The methods in this family share the fundamental goal of minimizing the photometric error between rendered images and ground truth inputs via gradient descent. All methods utilize differentiable volume rendering to compute gradients with respect to the neural network parameters. Common structural elements include the use of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to map spatial coordinates and viewing directions to density and color, and the use of ray sampling strategies to query these networks. However, the specific activation functions, sampling densities, loss formulations, and optimizer settings vary significantly to address artifacts like aliasing, dark pixels, or memory constraints.

## Subtopics

### [Mip-NeRF Optimization and Activation Details](3409-mip-nerf-optimization-and-activation-details.md)
This configuration defines the specific hyperparameters, activation functions, and input preprocessing steps used to train Mip-NeRF and JaxNeRF models. It sets itself apart from standard NeRF configurations by replacing the identity concatenation in MLP inputs with pure Integrated Positional Encoding (IPE), using shifted softplus and widened sigmoid activations for density and color respectively, and employing a specific warmup learning rate schedule. It builds on [Method-Specific Training Configurations](6267-method-specific-training-configurations.md). See [Mip-NeRF Optimization and Activation Details](3409-mip-nerf-optimization-and-activation-details.md).

### [NeRF-SR Training Configuration](15560-nerf-sr-training-configuration.md)
NeRF-SR is a training configuration designed to generate high-resolution (HR) novel views from low-resolution (LR) input images by optimizing a neural radiance field to match the LR observations while implicitly learning HR details through a supersampling strategy. It distinguishes itself from standard NeRF training by decoupling the training resolution from the rendering resolution, allowing the model to learn fine-grained texture details that are lost in standard LR training, and from post-processing upsampling methods by maintaining 3D consistency across views. Unlike Super-NeRF, which couples the NeRF with a GAN-based 2D super-resolution backbone and per-view latent codes, NeRF-SR relies on a deterministic supersampling strategy and an optional patch-based refinement network to enhance texture sharpness. See [NeRF-SR Training Configuration](15560-nerf-sr-training-configuration.md).

### Tri-MipRF Training Configuration
Tri-MipRF uses a tri-linear mipmap representation for efficient anti-aliasing. The base mipmap shape $M_{l0}$ is $H=512, W=512, C=16$. It employs the AdamW optimizer with weight decay $1 \times 10^{-5}$ and learning rate $2 \times 10^{-3}$, scheduled by MultiStepLR. The Tri-Mip encoding learning rate is scaled up 10x relative to the MLP. It uses an area loss $L_{area}$, scaling pixel loss by the area of its footprint on the image plane. Implementation uses PyTorch with tiny-cuda-nn and nvdiffrast [S1].

## Background
The need for mip-aware representations arises from the aliasing artifacts inherent in standard NeRF training when scenes are viewed at varying scales or resolutions. Mip-NeRF introduced integrated positional encoding to address this [S1]. NeRF-SR extends this concept to super-resolution tasks [S1]. Tri-MipRF introduces explicit mipmap structures for efficient anti-aliasing [S1].
